scope: Accelerated local campaigns with the optional callback adapter. Full samples, independent persisted-state audits, resource samples, and diagnostic profiling are kept separate.

implementation.environment: Same shared Docker host as the failed baseline runs: five visible CPUs and 33.29 GiB host memory. No resources were added and no per-container CPU/memory limits were configured. The historical 1,000-device demo continued sending periodic callbacks after its campaign completed. New fleet runs were sequential and unprofiled. Dependencies remained frozen; both runtime images used Python 3.12.16, with different base-image build timestamps.
implementation.buildNote: The cloud proxy CA was supplied as a BuildKit secret through a temporary external Dockerfile for dependency downloads. The repository Dockerfile was unchanged and TLS verification stayed enabled.

tests.environment: Docker with dedicated PostgreSQL16 firmware_test database

conditions.note: Shared cloud development environment. An existing 1,000-device demo continued sending periodic callbacks. The 2,000- and 5,000-device campaigns ran sequentially. Docker-visible CPU and memory values describe the host, not dedicated per-service allocations.
conditions.simulator: Supplied simulator with optional duplicate-response adapter
conditions.timing: Accelerated demo; no Docker build/startup included in campaign runtime

failedBaselines.important: Halt time is not a completion runtime. Neither new larger-fleet run completed. A later audit can show more resolved attempts than the runner's last sample.

runs.finding: A callback ReadError followed an accepted Download. One device had no qualifying BOOT or TransferComplete, despite later PERIODIC reports of the target version. The transport-error origin was not established.

Five attempts exceeded the 120-second result deadline and subsequently resolved through BOOT or TransferComplete. Their ACK delays ranged approximately 62–147 seconds. The campaign remained HALTED with 4,714 pending devices; the later audit found zero held slots and unknowns. The simulator saturated approximately one CPU core; the subsequent investigation identifies its HTTP pool bottleneck.

failedBaselines.conclusion: At revision 6ad4a1c, configuration supported the larger fleets, but neither baseline campaign completed under the unchanged accelerated settings. Those observations did not justify linear runtime claims from the successful 1,000-device runs.

before.caveat: Diagnostic cProfile adds overhead. Do not treat profiled duration as campaign benchmark.

after.caveat: Diagnostic cProfile only; duration/workload completion differs from baseline, not a throughput benchmark.

diagnosticProfiles.comparisonLimit: cProfile adds overhead. Different profile durations and completed request counts prevent using these figures as a campaign speedup ratio.

syntheticClientExperiment.scope: Isolated, instrumented HTTPX client experiment; separate local asyncio HTTP server; no controller/database;5000 callback-shaped POSTs jittered uniformly over30seconds;fixed50ms server delay; client uses localhostDNS; cProfile enabled inallcompletedcases. Shared host, not a production throughput benchmark.

ackLatency.definition: Controller dispatched_at to first persisted ACK received_at; includes delivery and processing, not pure network latency

groundTruth.scope: Simulator diagnostic ground truth from runner after monitoring; never used by controller to determine outcomes.

metrics.scope: Process-lifetime counters since fresh service startup; final scrape may include activity just after campaign completion.
metrics.histogramQuantiles: p99UpperBucketSeconds is the first cumulative bucket containing99% of observations, not an exact percentile; +Inf means no finite upper bucket.

resources.units: Docker CPU100% equals approximately one CPU core. Memory is Docker-reported usage in MiB; values reflect samples, not continuous peaks.
resources.method: Unweighted mean and nearest-rank p95 across periodic samples; shared host, not dedicated resource capacity or a hardware guarantee.

limitations: One accelerated simulated campaign on a shared development host; no real firmware installation or hardware capacity guarantee.
Campaign elapsed time excludes Docker build/startup. Database audit can follow the runner's last sample.
Resource maxima are sampled; histogram percentiles are bucket upper bounds, while ACK percentiles are computed from persisted event timestamps.
